title: Rethinking Molecular Text Representations for LLMs: An Empirical Study
abstract: arXiv:2606.03057v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for molecular tasks, but it remains unclear which molecular representation to use. We present a systematic benchmark, MolRepBench, to evaluate LLM molecular competence across nine representations and eight chemical tasks. We benchmark 16 LLMs across five model families, including reasoning and non-reasoning variants, chemistry-specialized LLMs, and closed frontier models. Performance is strongly representation-dependent and no single representation wins across tasks, though CML is the best, followed by MolJSON, InChI and canonical SMILES. Explicit structured text representations (CML and MolJSON) dominate structural tasks; IUPAC dominates semantic tasks, winning molecule retrieval for all 16 LLMs; and SMILES variants are rarely optimal despite their prevalence in pretraining. Chemistry-specialized models perform well with SMILES at the cost of large degradations with structured text

translated_title: 重新思考大语言模型的分子文本表示：一项实证研究
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在分子任务中的应用日益广泛，但究竟应使用哪种分子表示形式仍不明确。我们提出了一个系统性基准MolRepBench，用于评估LLM在九种分子表示和八项化学任务上的分子能力。我们对来自五个模型系列的16个大语言模型进行了基准测试，包括推理型与非推理型变体、化学专业LLM以及闭源前沿模型。结果显示，模型性能高度依赖于表示形式，且没有一种表示在所有任务上都占优，其中CML表现最佳，其次是MolJSON、InChI和标准SMILES。显式结构化文本表示（CML和MolJSON）在结构类任务中占主导地位；IUPAC命名法在语义类任务中占优，在全部16个LLM的分子检索任务中均获胜；而SMILES的各种变体尽管在预训练中被广泛使用，却很少是最优选择。化学专业模型在使用SMILES时表现良好，但使用结构化文本时性能会大幅下降。
tldr: 本文提出了系统性基准MolRepBench，通过对16个LLM在九种分子表示和八项化学任务上的评估，发现LLM的分子任务性能强烈依赖于表示形式且无通用最优解，其中CML整体最佳，结构化文本表示主导结构类任务而IUPAC主导语义类任务，SMILES变体虽在预训练中普遍使用却很少最优。
en_tdlr: MolRepBench, a systematic benchmark of 16 LLMs across nine molecular representations and eight chemical tasks, reveals that LLM molecular performance is strongly representation-dependent with CML being best overall, structured text representations dominating structural tasks, IUPAC winning all semantic retrieval tasks, and SMILES variants rarely optimal despite their prevalence in pretraining.
